{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / Customer "AP")

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Review of Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14), dated 5 February  
**Position:** We represent the Customer ("AP").

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is favourable to us: the arrangement is expressly non-exclusive, there is no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-solicit, no liquidated damages or exit penalty, no vendor audit right over us, and the vendor gives a broad, continuing performance warranty plus a strong defence-and-indemnity obligation with no cap applied to it. Assignment, termination for convenience and governing law/venue all sit at or above the playbook fallback and we are not redlining them.

Six items require attention. Two are critical: (i) there is **no intellectual property or ownership article at all**, so nothing confirms that we retain our Content, Properties and audience/visitor data, and nothing limits the vendor's use or monetisation of that data; and (ii) there is **no monetary limitation of liability anywhere** — Section 7 excludes consequential damages only, leaving both parties' direct liability unlimited, which fails even the fallback. In addition, the platform licence is expressly **revocable at the vendor's discretion** and does not extend to our affiliates or contractors; the post-Initial-Term exit notice is **90 days**, above the 60-day fallback ceiling; there are **no transition-assistance or data-return obligations** despite the vendor storing our data; and there is **no insurance covenant** for a vendor that hosts the platform and processes our data.

We have prepared redlines for each of the six. Everything else is closed.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble (no ownership article; related language at §9 warranty, licence grant, Content liability, trademarks) | No ownership clause; no purpose limitation or bar on monetising visitor data. Redline proposed. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | Preamble (§7; §§9–10 contain no cap) | Consequential-damages exclusion only; no monetary cap — direct liability unlimited both ways. Redline proposed. |
| 3 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble (§10(a), §9(b)(i), §11, §7(a)) | Meets preferred position; indemnity uncapped. Reciprocal breadth and Creative knowledge-qualifier noted only. |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble (¶2; ¶5(a); ¶4(c)(ii); ¶12(h)) | Grant is "revocable" with no termination trigger and excludes affiliates/contractors. Redline proposed. |
| 5 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble (¶(h); termination provision) | Free assignment to affiliate/asset purchaser/successor; no change-of-control or deemed-assignment trigger. Mutuality noted only. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Services clause, §1) | Exclusivity expressly disclaimed; we may sell Inventory through other agents. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble (§1; §6(a)) | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; §6(a) limits are standard software-licence protections. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | Preamble (¶4(a), ¶4(c), §5, §7) | No LDs, minimum fee or exit fee; notice-period revenue share is earned compensation. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (fallback) | Preamble (¶4(a), ¶5) | 1-year Initial Term; 90 days' mutual convenience notice thereafter, within the 60–90 day band. Revisit if term becomes multi-year. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal / non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | Preamble (auto-renewal and 90-day notice in ¶4) | 1-year auto-renewals acceptable, but the 90-day exit window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling. Redline proposed. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Preamble (§4(c), incl. 4(c)(iv)) | Only cessation, licence revocation and "return or destroy" of Confidential Information; no transition, export or certified deletion. Redline proposed. |
| 12 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | Preamble (§9(b); §13 disclaimer) | Continuing Term-long warranties; disclaimer is carved back for express warranties. No exclusive-remedy clause, so we keep full remedies. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | Preamble (§14(a); §8) | Delaware law (fallback) with exclusive New York venue (our preferred forum). §8 AAA arbitration tension flagged below. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble (§1 cooperation/access; Impression measurement) | No vendor audit, inspection or records right over us — better than preferred. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | Preamble (§5; §1) | No parity or rate-matching obligation in either direction. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble (§5; §1; "Winning Bid Price" definition) | Pure revenue share; no minimum spend, volume or take-or-pay on us. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble (independent contractor and confidentiality provisions; miscellaneous block) | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble (General Provisions; §9 data warranty) | No insurance covenant for a hosting vendor that stores our visitor data. Redline proposed. |

*All findings were recorded against the Preamble locator because the operative text is a single body section; the parenthetical clause references above are those identified in the underlying analysis.*

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our analysis places in, or adjacent to, walk-away territory. We should not sign as drafted.

1. **Licence revocable at the vendor's discretion (¶2).** The grant is expressly "revocable" with no limitation to a termination event, allowing the vendor to pull our platform access at will. This is walk-away territory under the licence rule; it also excludes our affiliates and contractors, and ¶5(a) bars third-party access absent the vendor's prior written approval, so there is no notice-based path to the fallback.
2. **No vendor insurance.** The vendor hosts the Auction Platform and, per its own warranty, collects, manages and stores visitor data. No insurance for a hosting/data-processing vendor is walk-away territory under the rule.
3. **No liability cap at all (§7).** Unlimited direct liability on both sides fails even the fallback (mutual 12-month fees cap). Because we pay no fees under the revenue-share in §5, a fees-only cap would be illusory, so the USD 1,000,000 floor is needed.
4. **Data deletion without return (§4(c)).** The bare "return or destroy" election for Confidential Information, with no export or transition obligation, risks the walk-away outcome of our data being deleted rather than returned.
5. **Non-renewal window at the threshold.** The 90-day post-Initial-Term notice exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling and sits **at** — not beyond — the walk-away threshold. Negotiable, but not acceptable as drafted.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the six redlines** with playbook comments:
   - **IP:** insert an ownership clause — we retain all rights in Content, Properties and Customer Data; the vendor keeps its platform and pre-existing tools; deliverables assigned with a perpetual, royalty-free licence back for embedded vendor IP; no joint ownership and no data monetisation.
   - **LOL-CAP:** add a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement uncapped as Excluded Claims, mirroring the carve-outs already in §7(a).
   - **LICENSE:** extend the grant to our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (with a matching carve-out in ¶5(a) and us responsible for their compliance), and make the licence revocable only on expiration or termination, consistent with ¶4(c)(ii).
   - **RENEWAL:** reduce the post-Initial-Term notice window to 30 days (fallback: 60 days) and confirm the notice also operates as non-renewal notice.
   - **TRANSITION:** insert new §4(c)(v)–(vii) — transition assistance, machine-readable data return within 30 days, and certified deletion (preferred six months' assistance; fallback 90 days).
   - **INSURANCE:** add a General Provisions subsection (j) at preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with USD 1M E&O / USD 2M cyber as the fallback.
2. **Resolve the dispute-resolution inconsistency.** §14(a) submits to exclusive New York court jurisdiction while §8 provides for AAA Commercial Rules arbitration. This is not a walk-away point (domestic AAA administration, no foreign seat), but the two provisions should be reconciled in one place under the dispute-resolution provision rather than duplicated in the governing-law clause.
3. **Diligence the Exhibits.** The fee/revenue-share Exhibits are not part of this document. They should be reviewed for any parity or rate-matching covenant (MFN), any customer-payable fees (which would re-open the termination-for-convenience refund and cap analysis) and any minimum volume commitment.
4. **Business team follow-ups (outside the playbook rules).** We have no express right to audit the vendor's Impression measurement or revenue-share reporting; if revenue assurance matters, raise a reporting/verification right. Separately, the vendor's use of visitor data is addressed only as a security warranty, which the IP redline is designed to fix.
5. **Re-review triggers.** If the term is extended to a multi-year committed term, revisit termination for convenience (add a 30-day customer convenience right with pro-rata refund and remove the vendor's mid-renewal-term exit)."}
